# `•explain` — Explain

`•explain text` runs `text` in the caller's scope, as `⍎` does, and gives a record of its result and of what happened while it ran:

- `value` is the result of `text`.
- `fused` has a row for each fused group that ran, as [`•prefs`](prefs.qmd) describes fusion. `glyphs` lists the glyphs of the group's calls in the order they ran. A fold that reads through the group, without building it, adds its glyph last. `items` is the group's item count. `blocks` counts the blocks of items that the group ran in turn. `runs` counts the pieces of work that those blocks split into. A block splits where it crosses the end of a long repeat or cycle in an input, as in adding a row of 5,000 items to every row of a matrix. More runs than blocks means the group ran in smaller pieces. `copied` counts the items copied out of inputs before the calls read them, as a reversed read needs. A `copied` of 0 means the group read every input in place.
- `stored` has a row for each pending array that a fused group read as an input after computing it on its own. `glyphs` gives the glyph of the call that computed it, which a copy, such as a reversal, doesn't have. `items` is its item count. `reason` says why the group didn't compute it as one of its calls:
  - `"held outside the graph"`: a name or another array also holds it, as `t` holds `t←y-0.25` in `t×1-t`.
  - `"read out of order"`: the group doesn't read item i of it at position i. Windows that overlap read some items more than once, and an outer product repeats each item.
  - `"kept by a fold"`: a fold left its calls in it, to compute later.
  - `"a different kind or width"`: it gives neither floats of the group's width nor a comparison of them, or its settings differ.
  - `"reads a comparison computed outside the graph"`: its call reads a comparison that something else also holds, or that has been computed already. The group would have to read that comparison's Booleans as floats.
- `forced` has a row for each call or assignment that computed items of pending arrays. Computing an array ends its fusion. `function` is the call's function, or `←` for an assignment that computed one by writing into it, displaying it with `⎕←` or destructuring it. `line` and `column` give its position in `text`, and `items` is how many items it computed. A selection of a few items, such as `↑r` or `2↑r`, reads a pending copy from its source and computes nothing. From a pending result that nothing else holds, such as `2×y+1` in `5↑2×y+1`, it computes only the items it reads. A pending result that a name holds is computed whole on its first read, and keeps its items for later reads.
- `fast` has a row for each [fast combination](../terms.qmd#term-fast-combination) taken, and for each fold of [windows](../glyphs/up-down-arrow.qmd) that slides over their source without building them. `combination` names it, and `function` is the function that took it. The names are `"partial grade"`, `"partial sort"`, `"ranks"`, `"group counts"`, `"group folds"`, `"determinant"`, `"permanent"`, `"masked select"` and `"sliding fold"`.
- `accumulations` has a row for each sum that added items at positions an index gave them, as the gradient of a selection that repeats positions does under [`∂`](../glyphs/partial.qmd), and for each modified assignment to a selection, as `z.[p]+←1` makes. `items` is how many items it added, and `size` is its result's item count. The gradients of reversal, rotation, take, drop, transpose, windows that move by 1, and `⌈` and `⌊` folds read the cotangent instead, and make no row. `path` names how the items were added:
  - `"in place"` adds into the array, with nothing to undo.
  - `"logged"` keeps each target's old item, to restore the array if a target fails. Exact integers take this path, because a sum can overflow.
  - `"on a copy"` converts the array first, as for 16-bit floats, or for exact integers that get floats.
  - `"rounds"` makes one call for each repeat of a position.
  - `"one call"` makes one call for targets at distinct positions.
  - `"item by item"` calls the function once for each target, as a dfn does.
- `fallbacks` has a row for each [map](../terms.qmd#term-map) that called its operand once for each cell after its [batched call](../evaluation.qmd#functions-and-effects) fell back, or without a batched call because an earlier one stopped. It also has a row for each time a batched call read its cells' items one at a time, through code with no rule for all the cells at once, even where the call then succeeded. `items` is the number of cells or items, and `reason` says why:
  - `"an effect"`: the operand writes output, reads input, formats a cell's value with `⍕`, or runs a system function other than a random draw. A batched call would do each of these once for all the cells. A random draw in a map inside the operand stops it too, and so does a random draw on a side of a guard on a cell's value.
  - `"a write"`: the operand writes to a name outside the map, or a side of a guard on a cell's value writes to a name outside its dfn.
  - `"a cell's value"`: the operand reads a cell's value to give a count or a position, as `2×⍣⍵` does. A predicate on a cell's value doesn't stop the batched call: each side of the guard runs once, on the cells that take it, as [Evaluation](../evaluation.qmd#functions-and-effects) describes.
  - `"no batch rule"`: the operand calls a function with no rule for batches of these arguments, such as `⍋`, or the two sides of a guard on a cell's value give results of different kinds or shapes. Where the stop comes from a primitive's call, the primitive's glyph follows, as in `"no batch rule for ⍋"`. A kernel that reads a cell's number directly, and `∂` with respect to cells that are arrays, give no glyph.
  - `"too many items"`: a call would repeat an array that every cell shares into far more items than its arguments hold.
  - `"a caught error"`: a guard would catch an error.
  - `"a recursive call"`: a guard on a cell's value runs in a recursive call of a dfn whose guard already split the cells, as in `{⍵<2?⍵;(∇⍵-1)+∇⍵-2}¨v`.
  - `"an earlier stop: "` and one of the reasons above: the operand is a dfn whose batched call stopped on an earlier call, for a cause that would recur, as [Evaluation](../evaluation.qmd#functions-and-effects) describes. The map calls it once for each cell without trying a batched call.
  - `"an error"`: the batched call failed. The calls on each cell then report the error, if one of them fails.
  - `"the result"`: the operand's result wasn't a batch of the cells' results, such as a function. A strand counts as one batch where each of its items holds an atom for each cell and the items' kinds join. So a strand that holds a vector for each cell falls back, and so does one that mixes numbers and characters.
  - `"item reads"`: code with no rule for batches read a batch's items one at a time.

Each of `fused`, `stored`, `forced`, `fast`, `accumulations` and `fallbacks` is a record of columns, as `•csv` gives a table, so `(•explain t).fast.combination` lists the combinations taken. `•prefs ["fusion":$t]` writes each forcing call and assignment as it happens. Nothing is recorded outside `•explain`.

```bpl
y←¿1000000⍴0
(•explain "+/(2×y+1.5)-1").fused            ⍝ ["glyphs":["+×-+/"] "items":[1000000]ₓ "blocks":[245]ₓ "runs":[245]ₓ "copied":[0]ₓ]
e←•explain "≢⍕(2×y+1.5)-1"
e.forced.function                            ⍝ ["⍕"]
e.fused.glyphs                               ⍝ ["+×-"]
(•explain "q←2×⌽y+1 ⋄ q≡q").fused.copied     ⍝ [1000000]ₓ
t←y-0.25 ⋄ (•explain "q←t×1-t ⋄ q≡q").stored  ⍝ ["glyphs":["-"] "items":[1000000]ₓ "reason":["held outside the graph"]]
(•explain "5↑2×y+1").forced.items            ⍝ [5]ₓ
s←2×y+1 ⋄ (•explain "5↑s").forced.items      ⍝ [1000000]ₓ
r←⌽y ⋄ (•explain "r.[0]←0").forced.function   ⍝ ["←"]
(•explain "(10↑)∘⍋ y").fast.combination     ⍝ ["partial grade"]
x←¿1000⍴0 ⋄ p←¿1000⍴1000
(•explain "{+/,(3↕⍵)×⍤1⊢1 2 1}∂ x").accumulations  ⍝ ["items":⍬ₓ "size":⍬ₓ "path":0⍴⊂""]
(•explain "{+/⍵.[p]}∂ x").accumulations            ⍝ ["items":[1000]ₓ "size":[1000]ₓ "path":["in place"]]
z←1000⍴0ₓ ⋄ (•explain "z.[p]+←1ₓ").accumulations.path  ⍝ ["logged"]
(•explain "{2×⍣⍵⊢1}¨⍳5").fallbacks  ⍝ ["reason":["a cell's value"] "items":[5]ₓ]
```

[`•memory`](memory.qmd) reports the live record nodes and pending arrays, and what a value keeps alive.
